ranked_evidence.title: ‘Corrupt bargain’ | Miller Center
ranked_evidence.snippet: Andrew Jackson received the most popular votes and the most electoral votes in the election of 1824. For the first time, the popular vote mattered—eighteen states were to choose their presidential electors by popular vote while only six states still left the choice up to their state legislatures. John Quincy Adams, 1824, by Thomas Sully, Metropolitan Museum of Art. Although John Quincy Adams should have been the heir apparent to the presidency as James Monroe's secretary of state, four other men also wanted to be President, each with substantial regional backing. Calhoun of South Carolina had served as secretary of war in the Monroe administration and had support from slave owners in the South. Although Adams was a centrist politician of sorts—a Jeffersonian-Federalist, to coin a new term—many Americans still identified him as a New Englander and as the son of the old Federalist leader John Adams.

ranked_evidence.title: 12 Political Putdowns (When 'Lowdown Crook' Isn't Specific Enough) | Merriam-Webster
ranked_evidence.snippet: *Kakistocracy* is one of those inexplicably uncommon words; a small bit of language that is so obviously useful that it boggles the mind that children are not taught this word in some early developmental stage, along with *cat*, *more*, and *mine*. It seems that a large number of people in every generation believe themselves saddled with a *kakistocracy*, and if we are being cynical (by which I mean realistic), they are probably all correct. In most cases, when one is confronted with the word *pornocracy*, one is also confronted by reference to the somewhat turbulent state of affairs in the Catholic Church in the early 10th century. Much of the use of *pornocracy* is directed at her, and the influence she was purported to have. However, it seems easy enough to use the word with a slightly relaxed meaning and to find it useful in describing all types of political states subsequent to the 10th century Vatican.
